title: Articulation Upper Bounds for Language Models
abstract: arXiv:2610.19721v1 Announce Type: cross  Abstract: Language captures only a subset of the perceptions, intuitions and intents that form meaning between speakers. What, then, are the limits of language? We take steps towards measuring this in LLMs as follows: for a set of concepts, we measure how well each concept can be transmitted between two LLMs as their capabilities scale. This requires novel measurement tools: (1) optimal messages: we introduce a prompt optimization algorithm that beats existing algorithms by up to 14% on benchmarks and accurately estimates prompt upper bounds. (2) A transmission measure: the sender is asked to label text; the receiver then tries to recover the sender's prompt, and recovery is measured; we find this correlates strongly with human label error. With these measures, we use observational scaling laws to study how transmissibility of a concept, conveyed with optimal messages, increases as transmitter and receiver capacity grows: does it asymptote below

translated_abstract: 语言只能捕捉说话者之间形成意义的感知、直觉和意图中的一部分。那么，语言的极限究竟在哪里？我们朝着在大语言模型（LLM）中衡量这一问题的方向迈出了步伐：对于一组概念，我们测量随着LLM能力的扩展，每个概念在两个LLM之间的传输效果如何。这需要新颖的测量工具：(1) 最优消息：我们引入了一种提示优化算法，在基准测试中比现有算法高出最多14%，并能准确估计提示的上限。(2) 一种传输度量：要求发送方对文本进行标注，然后接收方尝试恢复发送方的提示，并测量恢复的程度；我们发现该度量与人类的标注错误强相关。利用这些度量，我们使用观察性缩放定律来研究：随着发送方和接收方容量的增长，使用最优消息传达的概念的可传输性如何提升——它是否会在某一水平以下渐近收敛……
tldr: 本文提出了新的提示优化算法和基于“提示恢复”的传输度量方法，用于研究随着大语言模型能力扩展时概念在模型间传输的上限，从而探究语言表达能力自身的极限。
en_tdlr: This paper introduces a novel prompt optimization algorithm and a prompt-recovery-based transmission measure to study the upper bounds of concept transmissibility between LLMs as their capabilities scale, probing the intrinsic limits of language expression.
